recaps.title: Arnie's got a moustache: the Nordiques go eight and oh, the Canucks win two straight, and McPherson scores four again
text: Arnie Jordan here, coming to you from row three at Jordan Arena, with the Rinkside Report. Sunday, November twenty-second. My nephew delivered the whiteboard. It came with one marker, with about forty minutes of ink, for three games of hockey. You see where this is going. And yes, that's something on my lip. We'll get to it.

The early game, the RegattaSport Nordiques at the J.E. Culp Habs. Brian Culp opened it. A Culp scoring for the Culp Habs. Then Moorzey tied it, Lawrence scored, and Lawrence scored again, with Commish helping on all three. Commish, three assists in the first and not a point after. Punched out at intermission. KP got one back, and Pulo made it four to two.

Moorzey made it five to two in the second. I drew a little trophy on the whiteboard. Big mistake. Dixon scored. JMAC came out for Trigg, and Cooke scored all by himself. Then the Nordiques got caught with too many men, Moorzey sat for it, and Clark scored on the power play, from Greg Penney and Cooke. Five all. Moorzey, five points on the night, and one power play for the other team.

In the third, Langlois put the Nordiques back up. Then Lawrence and Brian Culp went off for roughing at the exact same second, and while they sat, Rob DeBolster scored. Seven to five Nordiques, final. Levar went the distance in the Habs net, and it was a long distance. Trophy erased. The Nordiques are eight and oh.

Here's a question for the comments under this report on the league website. Nordiques, was blowing a five to two lead part of the plan? Habs, how do you come back from three down and still lose? I read every comment, and I write back.

Game two, the Timbit Senators at The Keg Canucks. Obie opened it, and Pundy tied it. Then the penalty box got busy: Rids, Snihur, McMillan and Schmidt, all in two minutes. Then I knocked my coffee onto the whiteboard and wiped out the first period. Didn't matter. It was one all.

Halfway through the second, both teams changed goalies at the exact same second. Buynink out, Shannon in. Rennie out, The Plug in. I'm calling it the goalie square dance. Swing your partner, out you go.

Obie put the Senators ahead, then went off for roughing. Rids went off for hooking again, and Tweedy scored on the power play. Two all. Rids, two hooks, one goal against. You're fishing in the wrong pond. Adam Short scored, and Goodie made it four to two. Then Tourcotte went off for hooking, and Davies scored short-handed anyway. Down a man, the Senators score. Four to three Canucks, final, two wins in a row! Obie, two goals, an assist and a roughing call, and still nothing to show for it.

The late game, Dawson's Oilers at the ColdBreak Leafs. Parsons opened it, and Pierce scored with nine seconds left in the first. Two nothing Leafs. I wrote LEAFS LEAD in big letters. You'd think I'd learn.

In the second, NoPants got one back. Then Steele went off for slashing, and the Oilers scored twice on the power play, forty-one seconds apart. Craigy, then McPherson. Steele, you set up the first goal of the game and then two more for the other team. Three to two Oilers.

Then the square dance again! Raimondo out, Dawson in, Mallet out, Rosie in, and NoPants off for slashing, all on the same second. McPherson scored late in the period, four to two, and my marker started squeaking.

In the third, Steele went off again, roughing, with Derrick DeBolster. Six minutes for Steele, tied with Rids for the most in the building. Then McPherson scored. Then McPherson scored again, fifty seconds later. Pierce got one back with fifty-nine seconds left, and it ended six to three. Pierce, nine seconds left, fifty-nine seconds left. Somebody tell him there's a middle part.

McPherson, four goals again. Last week, four and a loss. This week, four and the boat stayed up. Craigy was on five of the six Oiler goals. Craigy, I've seen fellas pass less at a potluck. And the marker died. The last three goals went on a napkin.

Now, about the lip. Yes, that's a moustache. I grew it for Movember, to raise a little awareness and a few dollars for men's health, and my nephew says it looks like a caterpillar that gave up halfway across. Here's the serious part, fellas. Men die on average about four and a half years earlier than women, largely for reasons that could have been prevented, and about one in eight men will be diagnosed with prostate cancer in his lifetime. So book that check-up you keep putting off, and check in on the fella beside you on the bench. If you want to chip in, the link is in the comments under this report on the league website.

The big board, eight games in. McPherson leads the scoring with twenty-four points, Moorzey is right behind him with twenty-three, and KP and Pierce are tied for third with twenty. In net, Dawson is on top at three twenty-four, Trigg is second at three thirty, and JMAC is third at three seventy-six. In the standings, the Nordiques are eight and oh, sixteen points, still perfect. The Oilers have eleven, the Habs and Leafs have seven, the Senators six, and the Canucks four. Look out, everybody. Well. Look a little bit out.

One more for the comments. Who gets the hot dog of the week: McPherson for scoring four, or Craigy for setting up four? Make your case under this report on the league website. I read every one, and I write back.

So that's your week. Twenty-eight goals, two square dances, and one dead marker. My nephew says next week, a laptop. I don't trust anything I can't spill coffee on. If I got your name wrong, or gave your goal to the fella beside you, take it up with the refs, the timekeeper, and how fast you guys skate out there. This has been Arnie Jordan with the Rinkside Report.

recaps.title: Arnie's on camera: eleven for the Habs, the Canucks' first win, and the Nordiques stay perfect
text: Arnie Jordan here, coming to you from row three at Jordan Arena, with the Rinkside Report. And this week, for the first time ever, you can see me! That's right, the Rinkside Report is on camera. The camera is my nephew's iPad, propped up on my coffee cup and held there with a roll of hockey tape. It took him forty minutes to find me the record button. So wave. Two of you, maybe three. Hi.

Sunday, November fifteenth. Last week my nephew said we try crayons, so I came with the notebook and the big box. Sixty-four colours! Thirty-seven goals. You'd think that's plenty. You would be wrong.

The early game, the J.E. Culp Habs against the Timbit Senators. Dixon opened it, Williams tied it, and Tuby put the Habs back up. Then, with two seconds left in the first, Greg Penney scored all by himself. Two seconds. That's not a goal, that's a doorbell ditch.

Then the Habs hit the buffet. KP, thirty-six seconds into the second. Holt got one back. Cooke. Deakin. Then Greg Penney, Tuby and Dixon, three goals in three minutes, and Chinner made it nine to three. By then I'd used red, blue, white, a second red, and Burnt Sienna. I don't know what Burnt Sienna is. Buynink came out of the Senators net for Shannon halfway through, and the Habs said welcome, here's six more.

In the third, Williams and Simon Murphy made it nine to six. Then Hunt, and Ort. Eleven to six, final. Tuby had five points. And Ort scored, set one up, and took three for roughing at the exact same second Schmidt took three for slashing. Those two weren't battling, they were synchronizing watches.

Game two, The Keg Canucks against Dawson's Oilers. Adam Short and Beckett put the Canucks up two nothing. Then the second period became the McPherson Show. McPherson from Mansion. McPherson again, tie game, and on that same second both teams changed goalies.

Snihur went off for tripping, and the Canucks scored anyway. Koke, short-handed, from Pundy and Goodie. McPherson got it back on the power play, three all. Then the Oilers got caught with too many men. NoPants hopped over the boards, Wall never came off, and HoundDog got to sit three minutes for the both of them. NoPants, Wall, it's a line change, not a carpool. Colin Murphy scored right after it ran out, from Adam Short and Wes Short. The Short to Short connection now comes with a Murphy extension.

McPherson tied it four all in the third. Four goals, every Oiler goal, and Mansion helped on all four. That's not a line, that's a two-man band. Then New Guy scored, and a minute later New Guy scored again. Six to four Canucks, and that's the Canucks' first win of the season! Somebody frame the score sheet. McPherson, four goals and a loss. That's catching four fish and the boat sinks. And Dawson gave up four in front of a team named after him. Nobody respects the landlord.

The late game, the ColdBreak Leafs against the RegattaSport Nordiques. Pierce scored twenty-seven seconds in. Brophy went off for hooking, and Lawrence scored short-handed anyway. Two short-handed goals in one night. I don't own a crayon for that. Then Pierce got the power-play goal, from Steele. Two to one Leafs.

In the second, Collini went off for slashing, and the Nordiques made it count. Rob DeBolster scored while he sat, and thirty-five seconds later Dykstra, three to two Nordiques. Collini, one slash, two goals against. Bad exchange rate. Mallet came out for Rosie, JMAC came out for Trigg, and Pulo made it four to two with fifty-eight seconds left in the period.

Langlois scored early in the third. Larry Penney got one back. Then Moorzey scored from Regular and Lawrence, and on that same second, Brophy went off for roughing. Brophy, up by three and you still needed a sit-down. Six minutes, most of anybody all night. Horton got one more for the Leafs, and that was it. Six to four Nordiques.
Somewhere in there, a clearing attempt went so high it rang off the clock. I didn't catch who shot it, and I'm not asking.

Now, a look at the big board, seven games in. The scoring race: McPherson leads with nineteen points, and right behind him, KP, Pierce and Moorzey are all tied at eighteen. Three fellas at eighteen. That's not a race, that's a traffic jam. In net, by goals against average, Trigg is on top at three twenty-two, JMAC is right behind him at three thirty-eight, and Dawson is third at three forty-two. The Nordiques' top two goalies share one crease, and they just swapped spots. Cozy.

And the standings. The Nordiques are seven and oh, fourteen points, perfect, and I'm running out of nice things to say. The Oilers are second with nine. The Habs and Leafs are tied with seven, the Senators have six, and the Canucks have two, both from last night. You've got to start somewhere, boys.

So that's your week. Eleven for the Habs, four for McPherson in a loss, and a New Guy who scored two and is still the New Guy. By the late game I was writing Nordiques goals in Mauve. My nephew says next week, a whiteboard. If I got your name wrong, or gave your goal to the fella beside you, take it up with the refs, the timekeeper, and how fast you guys skate out there. Tape your sticks. This has been Arnie Jordan with the Rinkside Report.
recaps.email_note: New this week: Arnie is on camera! For the first time, you can watch him read the Rinkside Report from row three, on his nephew's iPad and a roll of hockey tape. Press play and say hi.

recaps.title: A Leafs winner with 36 seconds left, nine for the Nordiques, and an Oilers comeback
text: Arnie Jordan here, coming to you from row three at Jordan Arena, with the Rinkside Report. Sunday, November eighth, and I came with a coffee and a brand new system. Two pens. Blue pen for goals, red pen for the penalty box. My nephew says that's how the professionals do it. My nephew is nine. Hold that thought.

The early game was The Keg Canucks against the ColdBreak Leafs. Adams opened it four minutes in, and Steele made it two nothing thirty-four seconds later. Then the Canucks answered with a genuine Short to Short connection. Wes Short set it up, Adam Short buried it. Bowen tied it. Then Larry Penney and Haroutunian scored forty-one seconds apart late in the first, and it was four to two Leafs.

The red pen got a workout too. Adam Short went off for roughing in the first, and Wes Short went off for slashing in the second. So the Shorts scored together and served together. And Steele, who scored twice on the night, took three minutes for a slap shot. In this league that's the one shot you are not allowed to take, and he took it anyway, like a fella ordering the one thing that's not on the menu. The Plug came in for Rennie partway through the second, and nobody scored in the whole period.

Then the third, and the Canucks woke up. Gates went off for tripping, and Colin Murphy scored on the power play, from Goodie and Beckett. Steele got it back. Then Leyenhorst, then Goodie with three twenty-eight left, and it's five all. The Leafs blew a two-goal lead three different times. Last week I kept a Leafs Lead Counter. This week I kept a Leafs Lead Shredder.

Last two minutes, within two goals, so it's stop time, and the clock stops on every whistle. Then Darren Horton, from Collini and Pierce, with thirty-six seconds left. Six to five Leafs. The Canucks pulled The Plug for an extra skater and threw everything at the net, and none of it went in. Rosie went the whole game in the Leafs net, which is more than you can say for any of their leads.

Game two, the Timbit Senators against the RegattaSport Nordiques, and the red pen had exactly one customer. Dykstra. Two trips in the first period. While he sat for the second one, Williams scored on the power play. One more and you're done for the night, Dykstra, so walk, don't skate. He scored seventy seconds into the third, so that's a goal, two assists and two trips. A full itinerary.

Goals for the Nordiques from Brophy, Moorzey, Rob DeBolster, Whetlam, Lawrence, Dykstra and Langlois. Seven different goal scorers, and it finished nine to four. Moorzey had four points, and Regular had three assists, which for a fella named Regular is anything but.

For the Senators, Williams had a hat trick, one of them all by himself, and lost by five. That's bringing a turkey to the potluck and finding out everybody else brought nine. And Shannon went the whole game in the Senators net and watched nine go by. Somebody get that man a rear-view mirror.

The late game, Dawson's Oilers against the J.E. Culp Habs. Crandles went off for hooking twenty-seven seconds in, and Foran scored on the power play, from Craigy and Wall. Abrams made it two nothing, from Brown and Grossi. Then Grossi took three minutes for unsportsmanlike conduct, abuse of officials. Grossi had something to say to the referee, and the referee had three minutes to say back. Tuby got the Habs on the board late in the first, from KP and Dixon.

The second period was all Habs. Hunt, KP, Clark and Jim Culp. Five in a row, five to two. Right as Culp's went in, the Oilers swapped Raimondo out for Dawson, and I knocked my coffee onto the blue page. So the blue page is now a brown page.

And then the Habs stopped scoring. Completely. Dawson didn't let in another goal all night. Derrick DeBolster got one back, from HoundDog and Craigy, and McPherson made it five to four, from Grossi. Then Greg Penney went off for hooking, and Craigy tied it, from Mansion, five seconds after Penney's penalty ran out. Five seconds. Penney barely had time to close the penalty box door behind him.

Down the other end, Levar took at least three pucks right off the face mask. I was starting to worry, and then I figured it out. The man was hungry. Somebody told him the canteen had puck burgers on special, and he was trying to order through the cage. Levar, buddy, they go in the glove.

Tied at the buzzer, so it's a shootout, and that's three weeks running. McPherson buried it. Six to five Oilers. Habs, you scored five straight and went home with nothing. Grossi, two assists and a talking-to. Somewhere in that game, a pass went the whole width of the ice and straight out the bench door. I didn't catch who threw it, and I'm not asking.

So that's your week: a Leafs Lead Shredder, a Short to Short connection, and a full itinerary for Dykstra. The blue pen is out of ink, the red pen is fine, and the blue page is brown. My nephew says next week we try crayons. If I got your name wrong, or gave your goal to the fella beside you, take it up with the refs, the timekeeper, and how fast you guys skate out there. Tape your sticks. This has been Arnie Jordan with the Rinkside Report.

recaps.title: Six Leafs leads, four for KP, and goalies who change on cue
text: Arnie Jordan here, coming to you from row three at Jordan Arena, with the Rinkside Report. It was Sunday, November first, the night after Halloween, so I came armed with a coffee, the notebook, and a pillowcase of leftover candy. Thirty-three goals, counting a shootout, and by the third period I was writing on a candy wrapper. This week I'm keeping a new tally in the notebook, and it's the Leafs Lead Counter. Remember that.

The early game was the J.E. Culp Habs against the ColdBreak Leafs, and Pierce scored first for the Leafs. Tick, that's one on the Leafs Lead Counter. KP tied it, Haroutunian put the Leafs ahead again, tick, number two, and KP tied it again before the end of the first. In the second, Larry Penney scored all by himself, tick, three. Greg Penney tied it, Fernick scored, tick, four. Greg Penney tied it again.

Then Mills scored with twelve seconds left in the second. Twelve seconds. Tick, number five. In the third, KP tied it, Haroutunian got his second, tick, six, and Hunt tied it again. Six leads! I ran out of room on the page and started a column on my wrist. And then the Habs finally went ahead for the first time all night, when KP scored his fourth goal of the game, with three twenty-three to go. Four goals. KP must have thought those two kids in the stands were secretly scouts for the big leagues.

But wait. With two minutes left, Bigger went to the box for interference. Now, Bigger had set up KP's third goal earlier in the period, and then he went and handed the Leafs a power play, and Pierce tied it seven all with a minute fourteen left. Pierce finished with two goals and two assists.

So, another shootout, two weeks running. And Greg Penney buried it. Eight to seven Habs. KP scores four, and Penney gets the last word. The Leafs led six different times, and went home empty-handed. Last week they came back from four down. This week they invented the opposite. Collini slashed somebody in the first, then said sorry with three assists. And Mallet and Rico both went the full game and gave up seven apiece. That's not a goaltending duel. That's a goaltending potluck.

Game two, Timbit Senators against Dawson's Oilers. Brown opened the scoring, from Mansion and McPherson, and the Oilers led. For twenty-four seconds. Then Hageman tied it, and Davies scored on his own. The first period went back and forth to three all, and Mansion had assists on all three Oiler goals. Then, in the third, he went to the box for body checking. You can't pass to anybody from in there, Mansion. I've checked.

The second period belonged to Davies. He finished his hat trick with twenty-five seconds left in it, and he set up two more, so that's five points. Williams also had five points, two goals and three assists. Partway through, both teams changed goalies at the exact same second. Buynink and Raimondo out, Shannon and Dawson in. Somebody is coordinating this. Shannon gave up one goal the rest of the way and picked up an assist on Williams' last goal. Last week a goalie had an assist. This week a goalie had an assist. Seven to four Senators.

Now, the late game. RegattaSport Nordiques against The Keg Canucks. Leyenhorst scored first, and the Commish tied it. A goal by the Commish. Nobody's going to review that one. And then, in the second, they did it again. McKay and Rennie out, Trigg and The Plug in, at ten forty-five, the same exact second. Two at once, twice in one night. That's choreography. Next week I'm bringing music.

Fissel and Rob DeBolster scored fifty-eight seconds apart late in the second, and Langlois made it four to one in the third. Whetlam set up three goals and scored none. Generous to a fault. Then Bowen woke up and scored twice in the last three and a half minutes, and the Canucks were one short. Four to three Nordiques. Not a single penalty in that whole game.
And now, a first for the Rinkside Report. After the late game, a few of the fellas stayed back to relive the highlights, and they invited me into the dressing room.

Cookie of the Nordiques went first. Quote: "We had a hell of a game today. They came back hard on us, but we felt confident the whole way." He called his goaltending very top notch, and said they wouldn't have won without it. Then he tried to give a teammate credit for a great pass, and could not land the name. The room pitched in, and we settled on Trigger. One, two, three, Trigger. Now, the fella in the Nordiques net goes by Trigg, so either the goalie is sneaking up for passes, or somebody needs a name tag. Whoever you are, Trigger, great feed.

Across the room, Dawson, who took over the Oilers net partway through the second, was honest about his night. An equipment malfunction pulled his focus, but he isn't hitting the panic button. Quote: "We're not gonna peak too early in the season." Patience, Oilers fans. Your goalie has a plan.

Then Pulo summed up the evening in one word: "Terrible." And in the very same breath: "We're the most optimistic team in the league." Terrible and optimistic. That's hockey. One sniper was still sore about a wrist shot that rang the bar loud enough to wake the Zamboni driver, set up by Moorzey. So close. And Rob DeBolster, who did find the back of the net, had teammates so excited they called it a field goal. Last week it was three strikes, this week a field goal. This league will play any sport but hockey.

So that's your week: four goals for KP, a Leafs Lead Counter that stopped at six, goalies who change on cue, and a dressing room full of quotes. I dropped three mini chocolate bars under the bleachers, and I'm not going down there. If I got your name wrong, or gave your goal to the fella beside you, take it up with the refs, the timekeeper, and how fast you people move out there. Tape your sticks. This has been Arnie Jordan with the Rinkside Report.

recaps.title: A shootout, a goalie with an assist, and a four-goal lead that went missing
text: Arnie Jordan here, coming to you from row three at Jordan Arena, with the Rinkside Report. Thirty-five goals this week, if you count the shootout, and I do. And I've been recognized. A lady one row down turned around and asked me if I was the podcast guy. I said yes. She said, oh, I thought you'd be taller. I was sitting down. It was Sunday, October twenty-fifth.

First, a word for the stripes. Shane and Chip had the whistles, three games back to back, and I'd bet they skated more miles than any team out there. They called eight penalties all night, and three of them went to the same man, which in this league means you're done for the night. More on him in a minute.

The early game was the Regatta Nordiques against Dawson's Oilers. Whetlam opened the scoring, from Langlois and Roy, and Craigy tied it late in the first, set up by McPherson and, I checked this twice, Dawson. The goalie. A goalie with an assist. That man passes better than half the fellas skating in front of him.

Now, I started a new page in the notebook, and at the top I wrote one word: Stuart. Two trips in the first period, and a hook late in the second. Three penalties, and in this league three is the limit, so Shane and Chip showed him the door. Three strikes and you're out. Wrong sport, same result. That left Brown to drop back onto the blue line and play defence for the rest of the night. Before all that, Craigy's tying goal came while Stuart was sitting in the box. Shorthanded. Craigy, cleaning up after his teammate like a fella with a mop at a wedding. The Nordiques kept Stuart company: Andersen and Pulo for tripping, and Whetlam for a high stick, so Whetlam had a goal and a penalty. The full combo meal.

McPherson put the Oilers ahead in the second, and Trigg came in to replace McKay in the Nordiques net. In the third, Pulo tied it and Lawrence put the Nordiques ahead, then McPherson tied it again with forty seconds to go. Tied at the buzzer, and in this league that means straight to the shootout. No overtime. One shooter a side, and if they both score or both get stopped, you go again. Moorzy is the one who buried it. Four to three Nordiques. McPherson had two goals and an assist and went home with nothing. That's baking the whole cake and getting handed a cracker.

Game two, the Culp Habs beat the Keg Canucks eight to three. Penney had the hat trick and an assist, Hering and Dixon each had a goal and three helpers, Clark had three assists, and Paul scored twice. Koke, McMillan and Adam Short scored for the Canucks. Halfway through, both teams changed goalies at the exact same second, again. Rennie and Rico out, The Plug and Levar in. Two weeks running. Next week I expect a dance number. And not one penalty all game. Shane and Chip either had the quietest hour of their lives, or they left their whistles in the car.

Now, I have to tell you about upstairs. Behind the glass, up top, that's where you'll find the fellas who already played. Hot dogs, pizza, and the story of the goal they scored an hour ago, which gets prettier every time. And every time their team scores down below, they pound on that glass like it owes them money, and they holler, and they cheer. And then one of them always turns around and asks, can they hear us down there? Fellas, I'm in row three, and I can hear you. I can hear you chewing.

Then the late game, the ColdBreak Leafs against the Timbit Senators, and friends, sit down. The Senators led seven to three in the second. Obie had two goals and two assists, Simon Murphy had two goals, and Deakin, Holt and Sheridan chipped in. Holt and Sheridan scored fifty-four seconds apart while Adams sat for tripping. I took out a pen, a pen, and wrote: Senators in a cakewalk.

The Leafs then scored seven in a row. Parsons got one late in the second, and Haroutunian scored forty-seven seconds into the third. Then Collini scored three goals in one minute and fifty-five seconds. A hat trick in less time than it takes me to climb to row three. Parsons scored again, and Darren Horton finished it all by himself with fifty-one seconds left. Ten to seven Leafs. Horton had five points, Parsons and Pierce had four each. Upstairs, the glass took a beating. And Senators, Halloween's next weekend. You got your fright in early.

So that's your week: a shootout, a goalie with an assist, a man with his own page in my notebook, and a four-goal lead that went missing. Thanks to Shane and Chip for keeping the peace, and for giving Stuart the early night. If I got your name wrong, or gave your goal to the fella beside you, take it up with the refs, the timekeeper, and how fast you people move out there. Tape your sticks. This has been Arnie Jordan with the Rinkside Report.

recaps.title: Two six-to-five finishes, two hat tricks and a goalie swap that looked like a fire drill
text: Arnie Jordan here, coming to you from row three at Jordan Arena, with the Rinkside Report. Welcome back to both of my listeners. It was Sunday, October eighteenth, and after a week off I showed up with a fresh notebook, two sharpened pencils and a large coffee. I left with half a notebook, one pencil, and a napkin covered in arrows. Thirty goals, three games, and two of them won by a single goal.

The early game was the Regatta Nordiques against the Culp Habs, and Fissel scored forty-five seconds in, set up by Regular. Hunt tied it for the Habs, then Regular scored one himself late in the first, and another in the second, from Brophy and DeBolster. With a name like Regular, you'd expect a regular night. Two goals and an assist? I'd call it premium.

The rest of that second period was a parade to the penalty box. Brophy went for hooking, Paul went for tripping, and DeBolster went for something the timekeeper wrote down so fast I couldn't read it from row three. Two Nordiques in the box in one period, and the Habs didn't score on either one. Somewhere in there a clearing attempt went so high I lost it in the lights. I believe it came down during the second game. I did not see who shot it, and I have decided not to find out.

Paul made up for his trip early in the third, making it three to two, but Moorzy and Fissel answered a minute and a half apart, with Roy setting up both. Hunt got his second, and that's how it ended, five to three Nordiques. Paul had a goal, two assists and a trip to the box, which in this league is what we call a full evening. Trigg went the distance and held the Habs to three.

Game two was the Timbit Senators against the Keg Canucks, and I started a tally of lead changes on my napkin. Davies scored late in the first, and Buynink stopped everything in that period, then handed the net to Shannon. One perfect period, and the rest of the night off.

Then came the second period, and I am still recovering. Seven goals. Williams went to the box for hooking ten seconds in. Ten seconds. I was still blowing on my coffee. Obie made it two nothing, and then the Canucks scored three in a little over three minutes: Pundy, Adam Short, and Leyenhorst. The Senators came back with Sheridan and Davies again, and Leyenhorst got his second to tie it at four. Around goal number six, my first pencil snapped clean in half.

Martin put the Canucks ahead to start the third, with a goal and three assists on the night. That's two leads for the Canucks, and they gave both of them back, which is very generous. Obie tied it, and Schmidt scored the winner all by himself, no assists, didn't ask anybody. Six to five Senators. And then, with forty-seven seconds left and his team down by one, Pundy went to the box for interference. Best seat in the house for the finish, I'll give him that. Better than row three. Murphy had three helpers, and Shannon gave up five and still got the win.

The late game was Dawson's Oilers and the ColdBreak Leafs, and it turned into a hat trick contest. Foran scored fifty-seven seconds in, then Horton and Grossi traded goals all first period. NoPants and Grossi made it four to two Oilers in the second, before Adams and Pierce tied it right back up. Then, halfway through the period, both teams changed goalies at the same moment. Raimondo and Mallet out, Dawson and Rosie in. I thought it was a fire drill. Rosie had been in net for exactly one minute when Grossi scored his third. Welcome to the game.

In the third, Misek went to the box for tripping, and forty-five seconds later Horton finished his own hat trick to tie it at five. Then McPherson scored the winner, unassisted, with five thirty-six left. Last week he had six points. This week he had one, and it was the one that counted. Grossi finished with five points. Horton and Pierce had four each, and the Leafs got nothing for it but a sore neck from watching the scoreboard.

So that's your week: thirty goals, two hat tricks, two six to five finishes, and a napkin with four lead changes on it, every one of them from game two. If I got your name wrong, or gave your goal to the fella beside you, take it up with the refs, the timekeeper, and how fast you people move out there. Tape your sticks, and wave if you see me in row three. This has been Arnie Jordan with the Rinkside Report.

recaps.title: Thirty-six goals, two six-point nights and one clean game
text: Arnie Jordan here, coming to you from row three at Jordan Arena, with the Rinkside Report, the only hockey podcast with two loyal listeners. Three, if my neighbour remembers. It was Sunday, October fourth. I had a coffee in one hand and a pencil in the other, and I needed both, because we had three games and thirty-six goals. Thirty-six. I ran out of page.

Game one was the Keg Canucks against Dawson's Oilers, and the Oilers put ten on the board in a ten to five win. From where I sat, Ron McPherson was everywhere, with two goals and four assists for six points. That's not a stat line, that's a phone number. Darren Craig had a goal and four helpers, and Mike Foran scored a pair. I will say there was one pass in that game that missed everybody on the ice, and I believe it is still on its way to Vineland. I didn't catch who threw it, and I'm not asking.

But give the Canucks their due. Down seven to two, they could have packed it in. Instead, Daryl Strong and Wes Short scored forty-five seconds apart to close out the second period, both set up by Waylon Tweedy and Kurt Peters, and Paul Koke had two of his own. I barely had the first one written down before the second one went in. The Oilers also took three trips to the penalty box and still won by five, so I'll keep my opinions to myself, at least this week.

Game two. I had just sat back down with a fresh coffee. The ColdBreak Leafs came out flying, with goals from Kevin Pierce, Larry Penney and Adam Steele, and they led three to one after the first period. I wrote the word upset in my notebook. I have since crossed it out, because the Regatta Nordiques scored eight in a row. Josh Moore had the hat trick and three assists, so that's six points for him as well. Doug Lawrence scored twelve seconds into the third, Moore scored again less than a minute later, and that was the hockey game.

Nine to three for the Nordiques, with two goals each for Lawrence and Nick Langlois, and four points for Adam Regular. And a tip of the cap to Kevin Rolston, who came into the Nordiques net halfway through and did not let in a single goal. He made it look so easy that I started wondering if I could do it. I could not. I get winded on the stairs up to row three.

Game three was the late one, the Culp Habs against the Timbit Senators, and the first period was a track meet. Drew Hering scored forty seconds in, before I had even sharpened my pencil, and then he got another. Matt Dixon added a third, and Kevin Paul set up all three of them. But every time the Habs scored, the Senators answered, with Blaine Davies, then Tyler Williams, then Davies again. It was tied at three after one.

After that, the Senators shut the door. Simon Murphy scored with fifty seconds left in the second and again in the third, and Rob Holt added one for insurance, for a six to three final. Davies and Murphy each had two goals and two assists, Dave Sheridan had three helpers, and Tim Shannon came in cold and stopped everything he saw. Somewhere in there, a shot went so wide that it rattled the glass right in front of me. I spilled half my coffee, and I would like the league to know that I am keeping the receipt.

And listen to this. There was not one penalty in that game. Sixty minutes of oldtimers hockey, and nobody went to the box. I keep a whole column in my notebook for penalties, and it is still empty. I didn't think it could be done.

So that's your week: thirty-six goals, two six point nights, and one game as clean as a whistle. If I got your name wrong, or gave your goal to the fella beside you, take it up with the refs, the timekeeper, and how fast you people move out there. All the details are on the league website. Tape your sticks, and give me a wave if you see me in row three on Sunday. This has been Arnie Jordan with the Rinkside Report.
